chunks: From him, from Ali, from Ismail ibn Mihran, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:

Regarding the Statement of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: 'And permission shall not be given to them so that they should offer excuses.' He said: 'Allah is more Majestic, Just, and Greater than that if a servant has an excuse, He would not allow him to present it. But rather, he would be defeated/ruin, so there was no excuse for him.'
ai.seo_question: Why does Allah prevent the disbelievers from offering excuses on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the divine wisdom behind the denial of excuses in the Hereafter, asserting that Allah’s absolute justice ensures no valid plea is ever overlooked. The inability to offer an excuse signifies that the individuals have exhausted all possible justifications, leaving them in a state of total defeat (fulij) with no remaining ground for defense. This interpretation underscores the precision of divine retribution, where the silence of the disbelievers confirms the completeness of their accountability.
